Archimedes Triangle

GeometryAreaTriangles
Game: Drag two points on a curved line to make a triangle, then see how much of it the curve fills. There is nothing to win or lose.
How to play: Drag the blue points A and B, or focus one and use the arrow keys. Tick Lemma and Theorem to reveal the hidden lines and points.

Drag A or B, or focus one and press the arrow keys (Shift for bigger steps).

Look for the math

Pick two points on a parabola. The two tangents there meet at S, and the chord AB is the base of the triangle ABS. Archimedes used this triangle to measure the curved cap cut off by the chord — over two thousand years before calculus.

A triangle made by tangents

Write a point of the curve as t steps sideways from the axis. With focal length a the point is (t, t²/(4a)) above the vertex, and its tangent has slope t/(2a). For the two points t₁ and t₂, solving the two tangent equations gives S = ((t₁+t₂)/2, t₁t₂/(4a)). The midpoint M of the chord has the same sideways coordinate (t₁+t₂)/2, so the line MS is straight up — parallel to the parabola's axis.

The three midpoints

The line MS meets the curve at O, which sits at parameter (t₁+t₂)/2. Its tangent is parallel to the chord AB. Where that tangent crosses the sides it lands exactly halfway: A1 is the midpoint of AS and B1 of BS. And O is halfway between M and S. Tick Lemma to see the axis, the focus and the two points under A and B; tick Theorem for the tangent at O and the two inner sides. The logic test checked all three midpoint claims on 413 configurations.

Why the curve takes two thirds

Set the area of ABS to 1. The inner triangle ABO takes 1/2. The cap above it takes 1/4, and the next four caps together 1/16; the total is a geometric series. Archimedes summed it as 1/2 (1 + 1/4 + 1/16 + …) = 2/3. So the parabolic segment is two thirds of the Archimedes triangle, whatever the two points you chose. The test measured the ratio on all 413 shapes; the largest departure from 2/3 was below 0.00000001.

About this port

The Java applet let the two points travel past the edge of its canvas and used whole-pixel coordinates, so near-parallel tangents could drift a few pixels; our handles stop while still in view and the drawing uses exact coordinates. The applet's "filled triangles" switch was only enabled after Theorem was ticked — that quirk is kept. The cut-the-knot address below now carries a GeoGebra illustration rather than the Java applet itself; it is the closest verified article describing the same lemma and theorem, so it is the one cited here.

Tick Theorem and Filled triangles, then drag A towards B: the pieces change size but the two-thirds ratio never does.
